product.industry: Humanoid robotics and embodied autonomy laboratory
product.audience: Operations leaders and research partners imagining a humanoid inside a real work environment
product.decision: Feel the machine's physical character, then test whether its movement and safety model fit a selected task
product.conversion: Choreograph a fictional first shift and log a field-evaluation request

signature.moment: A life-scale 3D humanoid wakes inside an orange spatial field, then changes gaze, stance and reach while giant type and safety geometry respond to the selected procedure

systems.hero: A borderless theatre of body, type and moving calibration geometry; the robot interrupts a two-line kinetic statement instead of sitting inside a dashboard cell
systems.navigation: A floating black instrument strip cuts across the bright stage and carries chapter, state and evaluation actions
systems.contentDensity: Alternating spectacle and compression: full-bleed spatial scenes, narrow score strips, quiet photographic pauses and one tactile ticket
systems.geometry: Oversized cropped type, diagonal floor axes, animated reach halos, hard photographic wipes and score notation
systems.motion: Explicit procedure changes send the body between poses; scroll moves type layers, floor axes and image masks without making content frame-dependent
systems.coreInteraction: Visitors direct teach, sense, carry and verify beats, then turn that choreography into a visible first-shift ticket

structuralDifferences: Mobile opens with a portrait body stage and the active verb overlaid at hand scale, not a compressed desktop split
The four-beat desktop score becomes a thumb-operated vertical cue stack whose active cue changes the code-native body pose
Full-width photography becomes swipe-like image chapters with visible step buttons rather than desktop wipes
Sensor and stopping stories use circular single-focus instruments instead of wide technical ledgers
The first-shift outcome becomes a tear-off ticket at the end of the flow

artDirection.typography: Massive compressed neo-grotesk as moving physical matter, contrasted with tiny monospaced score notation; no repeated editorial-serif formula
artDirection.material: Safety orange field, warm composite shell, absolute black, laser cyan, aluminium and scuffed industrial photography
artDirection.imageLogic: Procedural 3D owns the theatrical body; three original photographs provide human scale, field consequence and tactile contact; CSS/SVG create the score and safety geometry
artDirection.microcopy: Wake, look, reach, carry, yield, stop, score, body, floor, first shift and field-note language
artDirection.dataHonesty: All cycle, reach, force and readiness values remain clearly fictional illustrative template data

interactions.name: Movement score
interactions.input: Choose tote, inspect or kit, then cue wake, look, reach and verify
interactions.stateChange: 3D joints, mobile body pose, reach object, sensor halo, active verb, floor geometry and cycle note change together
interactions.visibleResult: The visitor directs an embodied four-beat performance rather than changing a dashboard value

interactions.name: First-shift ticket
interactions.input: Choose floor, carried object and shift rhythm, then provide evaluation contact details
interactions.stateChange: Ticket number, readiness, safety mode, scene color and confirmation stamp update
interactions.visibleResult: A theatrical but useful commissioning ticket resolves from the movement choices

assetStrategy: The existing three original local frames are re-authored as a film sequence rather than evidence cards: arrival in the lab, movement in the field and touch at the object.

adjacentTemplates.why: Both pursue cinematic energy, but PULSE carries one can through three photographic worlds and a bag flow; robotics directs an articulated body through a movement score and commissioning ticket.
A bright performance stage, image curtains and movement verbs replace dark mission telemetry, orbital deployment and coverage planning.
The visual system behaves like body choreography and theatre, not a broadcast timing wall or strategy simulation.
Life-scale movement and image wipes replace radial micro-mechanics, exploded layers and collector configuration.
A machine body follows task and safety cues rather than assembling cloth silhouettes or runway looks.
